speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) whether an update can be provided regarding the CPIB investigation into Seatrium; (b) whether the investigation pertains to the predecessor entities of (i) Sembcorp Marine and (ii) Keppel Offshore and Marine; (c) what measures are being taken to ensure that individuals will be brought to justice in the event of offences being made out; and (d) what is the assessed impact to Singapore's reputation (i) in general and (ii) in the jurisdiction or region where the alleged offences took place.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Prime Minister regarding CPIB's investigation into Seatrium and individuals from the company (a) what is the number of current and former employees of the company being investigated and whether they are based in Singapore; (b) whether the decision by Temasek Holdings to inject capital into then-Sembcorp Marine took into account the alleged corruption offences that occurred in Brazil; and (c) whether CPIB is working with the Comptroller General of Brazil on the preliminary administrative liability proceedings against the company's subsidiary.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
text: I invite Mr Pillai to raise any supplementary questions that he may have today and to withdraw his Parliamentary Question for tomorrow if his queries have been addressed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: CPIB will be interviewing various individuals of interest and reviewing all documentary and other records to which it can gain access.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Other than CPIB, we understand that the Brazilian authorities are investigating Seatrium, but it would not be appropriate to provide any details or comments at this juncture.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It will investigate the case thoroughly and seek to complete the investigations expeditiously.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng asked about the assessed impact on Singapore's reputation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As CPIB's investigations are still ongoing, it would be premature to speculate on the outcome.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Louis Chua asked whether the decision by Temasek to inject capital into then-Sembcorp Marine took into account the alleged corruption offences in Brazil.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Temasek became a direct shareholder of Sembcorp Marine in 2020 following the demerger of Sembcorp Marine from its then-parent, Sembcorp Industries.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Temasek participated in Sembcorp Marine's two rights issues in 2020 and 2021.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government understands that Temasek conducted the due diligence appropriate to the rights issues, bearing in mind that the company was already part of the group.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This due diligence took into account Sembcorp Marine's public disclosures that had already been made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The disclosure pertaining to the Brazilian case mentioned that there were charges by Brazilian authorities against an ex-employee in his personal capacity and not against Sembcorp Marine's Brazilian subsidiary or the company.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Sembcorp Marine Group also stated it was not aware of any other of its employees being subject to those investigations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: All disclosures in the circulars and Offer Information Statement came with a representation by Sembcorp Marine's board on the accuracy of information and that all material disclosures had been made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Temasek's investments in Sembcorp Marine pursuant to the rights issues, as well as those of all other investors, were based on the information provided in the shareholders' circulars and Offer Information Statement.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the Sembcorp Marine Group's announcements on 3 July 2019, 8 July 2019, 3 February 2020 and 21 February 2020, it further stated that it was committed to the highest standards of compliance with anti-corruption laws and does not condone, has not condoned and will not tolerate any improper business conduct.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The rights issues were raised during the pandemic to ensure that Sembcorp Marine had sufficient funding to see through its business obligations and complete existing projects, given the downturn of the industry which was exacerbated by COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Without the recapitalisation, there would potentially have been an erosion of value and a loss of jobs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: At the time, I said, "If a prominent company, especially one linked to the Government, fails to uphold the law and proper standards of conduct wherever they are, it hurts our national reputation." Can I ask the Minister whether she agrees that we have to maintain Singapore's reputation for zero tolerance against corruption?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My second question to the Minister is: have CPIB and the Government considered the use of bounties or rewards for whistleblowers and tipoffs that lead to a conviction?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I note that the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore recently offered a reward for whistleblowers who report tax evasion.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Would CPIB consider a similar approach, especially for cases where Singapore's reputation is at stake?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The short answer to the first question is absolutely.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But part of the consideration or the factors that must be taken into account are these: do you want to incentivise reporting with the lure of gain of a reward?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Or do you want a system where people whistleblow or make the report or complaint because, fundamentally, they feel that something is wrong and it is the right thing for them to do – to make the report or bring this to the attention of the authorities?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think that is the balance that we need to maintain.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And if it were possible to maintain a system where people file reports because, as a matter of principle, they feel that something is wrong, that means that we would have a healthy system, where there is a strong sense of right and wrong in the community and in business circles, and people do the right thing.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In the interest of good stewardship and given that it is Singapore's reputation at stake, how does the Ministry of Finance (MOF) and Temasek ensure that there are adequate anti-corruption and bribery controls that are put in place, that these are effectively enforced and that Temasek, as a shareholder, has effective oversight over these risk mitigation strategies and controls?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, he had asked about MOF and Temasek.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have got strong laws on that and do not hesitate to enforce if need be.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That, obviously, is communicated to all companies in which the Government either owns or, in fact, companies which the Government does not own.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They, too, send a strong signal that corruption is not to be endorsed, encouraged or in any way acceptable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The thing to remember about corruption though is that, by its nature, it is done in secret.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I mean, unless they are not very adept, nobody goes around actively publicising that you are doing a corrupt activity.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Fraud and corruption, by their very nature, tend to be secret.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the key thing here is to continually review processes to see whether your processes are robust and enable something to be flushed out if need be.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And even then, as we have seen in many other cases, it is not 100%.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the short answer is that we just need to continue to be active, vigilant, get the message out and, as Temasek has said, keep continuing its regular engagement with companies and setting the standards.
